title: Albatross Fleet deploy ops scratchbook
content:
Context:
Albatross Fleet (customer) — mid-market logistics provider, ~1.2k vehicles across US/EU. They want an operational assistant that summarizes driver telematics, flags exceptions, and answers short natural-language queries about routes and incidents. Target: hybrid private deployment (VPC) with occasional burst to Dedicated. Data is PII-lite but with license plates/driver IDs — customer requires KMS integrations and audit logs.

Call notes (2025-02-10 sync with Albatross eng and ops):
- Attendees: Megan (Albatross SRE), Carlos (product), Sofia (ops), Maya (Redwood SE), Luca (Redwood infra).
- High-level ask: near-real-time summaries of inbound telemetry (GPS, speed, diagnostics) + natural-language Q&A for ops staff.
- Volume estimate: 1,200 vehicles sending ~1 message/minute average, spikes during shift changes ~3x; typical payloads small (200–600 bytes).
- Query pattern: 25–50 interactive queries/sec during peak support windows; many queries short (utterance length ~12 tokens), but summary generation ~200–600 tokens per doc.
- Latency SLO: interactive Q&A <300ms p95, long summaries allowed up to 2s p95.
- Security: must run in customer VPC with private control plane; HSM-backed keys (customer uses AWS KMS + external HSM for some keys).
- Retention/compliance: 90 days of audit logs; telemetry stored in their S3 bucket, Redwood should not persist raw telemetry outside ephemeral inference cache.

Technical constraints & observations:
- Network: Their edge collectors are NATed behind carrier networks; keep-alive and TLS 1.2 supported but they have legacy proxies that mangle SNI occasionally. Potential gotcha: our auto-routing by region might prefer eu-west which breaks due to proxy SNI — need explicit routing config for their collectors.
- On-device preprocessing: they want lightweight protobuf->json conversion at edge, with hashing of plate numbers before sending (customer will provide salt). Confirmed this is fine, but note: hashed identifiers reduce ability to join to their historical DB unless we sync salts/keys.
- Throughput patterns: 1,200 msgs/minute baseline ~20 rps, spike windows up to 60 rps ingestion. Downstream inference load roughly 0.2 inference per message (only ~20% trigger summaries), plus separate interactive query pool 25–50 qps. So plan capacity for ~40–70 inference rps with burst headroom to 150 rps.
- Caching: prefix and KV caching for repeated queries (e.g., many agents ask same hotspot question) will reduce costs. Recommend TTL 10m for hotspot queries; implement per-driver cache key.
- Model choices: prefer a smaller instruction-tuned open model for interactive Q&A (latency-sensitive) and a larger summarization model for batch/long summaries. Plan: hosted catalog candidate for PoC: small LLaMA-variant 7B quantized on Dedicated for p95 <300ms for short queries; A100-backed dedicated for 13B-type summarization if customer elects.
- Quantization: they prefer int8/4 to reduce cost. Need to validate quality for summary coherence on telematics text — include eval set.

Integration gotchas (from the call + follow-ups):
1) TLS/SNI proxy bug: during initial test the collector dropped connections to our default gateway. Workaround: allow their gateway IPs and route to eu-central instead of eu-west; also provide HTTP fallback for batch ingestion temporarily. Action: Luca to add route exception (due 2025-02-14).
2) Tokenization surprises: telemetry blobs include VIN-like strings that the tokenizer splits badly and increases token count for summaries. Mitigation: preprocess VINs to hashed placeholders; confirm with product if VINs are necessary in summaries.
3) KV cache cold start: first-day burst will be heavy because vehicles restart after OTA; recommend warmup run (run replay of last 24h telemetry through cache warmup job).
4) Audit log format: Albatross wants per-request user_id and vehicle_id in logs. We need to include hashed driver_id in request metadata and ensure it lands in the control-plane audit event. Confirmed support but need schema mapping.

Action items / next steps:
- Maya: produce a minimal PoC architecture diagram + cost sketch for two modes (PoC: Dedicated small pool + Private control-plane; Scale: Private + Dedicated+burst). Target delivery: 2025-02-13.
- Luca: add route exception and test connectivity with their NATed collectors; validate TLS fallbacks. Due: 2025-02-14.
- Priya: assemble evaluation prompt set (50 real telemetry snippets + expected summaries) and run quality checks on 7B quantized and 13B float. Due: 2025-02-18.
- Megan (customer): provide anonymized telemetry sample (last 72h) and the salt for plate hashing. Due: 2025-02-16.
- Operations: schedule a warmup job to replay sample into cache when PoC cluster is provisioned. Owner: Albatross ops + Redwood infra (joint). Tentative window: after PoC provisioning.

Test plan (PoC):
- Connectivity: 6h soak test from a subset (50 vehicles) through existing proxies to Private control plane gateway in eu-central. Verify no connection drops for 24h.
- Latency: synthetic queries (n=10k) to measure p50/p95 p999 for interactive model; target p95 <300ms.
- Correctness: run 50 telemetry->summary pairs; measure ROUGE/L and manual review for hallucination.
- Security: KMS key rotation test (rotate test key and ensure infra still decrypts), audit event ingestion verified for 90-day retention.

Prompt examples & eval snippets (quick):
- Short query (interactive):
  User: "Why did vehicle 479 stop on 2025-02-09 14:12 UTC?"
  Context (metadata): lat/lon breadcrumbs, speed from last 10s, diagnostics flags: engine_temp_high.
  Expected: "Vehicle 479 decelerated to stop likely due to engine overheating (engine_temp reading exceeded threshold at 14:11), recommended inspection; no collision flag present."

- Summary generation (long):
  Input: 8-minute telemetry window with repeated engine_temp spikes, reduction in speed, and intermittent connectivity.
  Expected: 4–6 sentence summary focusing on repeated overheating, probable cause, timestamps, recommended next steps, risk severity = high.

Notes to self / informal: 
- Keep PoC minimal: avoid running customer data through hosted API in this phase. Private control plane is required.
- Need to add a short blurb on token cost vs. latency trade-offs for the 7B quantized model — helps SRE justify Dedicated pool sizing.
- Remember to capture default fallback policy: when private capacity saturated, automated routing -> Redwood-hosted compatible model in different tier (customer must opt in). Document opt-in form.

Meeting cadence proposed:
- Weekly sync (30m) with Albatross engineering ops (Wednesdays) for first 6 weeks.
- Ad-hoc deep-dive with security (Redwood) during integration window.

Open questions to resolve quickly:
- Does customer accept hashed vehicle IDs for correlation with their historical analytics? If not, propose secure token exchange protocol.
- Which summarization model family are they prepared to accept for initial PoC (cost vs quality)? Need a yes/no by 2025-02-17.

Quick timeline sketch:
- 2025-02-13: Architecture + cost sketch (Redwood)
- 2025-02-16: Customer telemetry + hashing salt
- 2025-02-18: Eval results and recommendation (Priya)
- 2025-02-24: PoC cluster provisioned and connectivity test
- 2025-03-03: Initial PoC review and go/no-go for scale

Random quick notes (scratch):
- Consider using short-circuit fallback policy to return cached summary for repeated queries in <30s window to keep p95 low during spikes.
- Add an opt-in toggle in console for "allow burst to Redwood-hosted" with clear SLA implications.

End of scratchbook entry.
